name: Palti
overview: Palti is a male figure in the biblical narrative identified primarily as the new husband of Michal, the daughter of King Saul. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribal affiliation or other personal notes. His mention is concise, focusing on his marital connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Palti means 'G-d is my deliverance,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names. A variant of his name, Paltiel, carries the same meaning and appears in related scriptural references, emphasizing reliance on divine deliverance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Palti's relationship to Michal as her husband. No other family relationships or lineage details are provided beyond this marital connection.
scriptureSignificance: Palti's significance lies in his marriage to Michal, which situates him within the complex narrative surrounding King Saul's family and David's rise. His role illustrates the personal and political dynamics of the time, particularly regarding Michal's marital status. Though not a central figure, Palti's presence marks an important relational detail in the biblical account.
